milestone.title: mp watch — automated milestone execution via herdr agent lifecycle

intent.outcome: Users can run `mp watch <milestone-id>...` and the daemon drives each milestone from its current state through to completion — spawning runner/coordinator agents via herdr, handling handoffs, reusing sessions across milestones, and logging everything. No manual intervention required.

problem.description:
Driving a milestone through its lifecycle (approved → in-progress → self-reviewed → review → complete) requires manual CLI commands and manual agent session management. The mp-flow/mp-runner/mp-coordinator skills document what to do at each stage, but no daemon automates the loop. Each handoff requires the agent to notice state changes in plan.json, start/stop sessions, and pass handoff data. There's no single `mp watch` command that someone can point at a milestone and walk away.

Meanwhile, herdr exists as an agent multiplexer that can spawn, observe, and manage agent sessions. The pieces are all there — mp for plan data and handoff recording, herdr for agent lifecycle, harness CLIs for execution — but they've never been wired together into an automated loop.

in_scope: `mp watch <ids...>` CLI command — accepts one or more milestone IDs, processes them sequentially
`[agent.runner]` and `[agent.coordinator]` config sections — harness type, model, thinking level per role
herdr integration: spawn panes via `herdr agent start`, send prompts, read output, wait for completion
Same runner and coordinator panes reused across sequential milestones (no restart between milestones)
Lifecycle state machine: detect current state, determine next action, execute, loop until done
Handoff data passing through plan.json (findings, evidence, AC status via `mp reviews handoff`)
Config validation on startup with clear error messages
`mp watch --dry-run` — print the execution plan without running anything
Structured logging to a configurable log file
Signal handling (SIGINT/SIGTERM) — graceful shutdown, marking in-flight milestones
out_of_scope: Cross-milestone dependency resolution (handled by `mp path` already)
Custom prompt templates per milestone type or per AC
Web UI, dashboard, or notification delivery
Non-herdr agent backends (tmux, direct subprocess) — herdr is the only supported runtime
Automatic milestone creation or grooming — only drives existing ready milestones

acceptance_criteria.description: After runner completes (lifecycle=self-reviewed), mp watch spawns a coordinator pane and sends the external review prompt. design_decisions.rationale: Model/harness/thinking_per_role are project-level preferences that should be consistent across sessions, not re-specified on every command.
Fewer moving parts. Future milestones can expose prompt templates as configurable files if needed.
herdr provides state rollups, herdr wait, pane read, and pane labeling. Keeping one backend simplifies the code.

design_decisions.choice: reuse same panes across milestones, don't restart
design_decisions.rationale: Avoids herdr sidebar clutter and preserves agent context between milestones.

design_decisions.choice: poll mp show milestone at configurable interval (default 1s)
design_decisions.rationale: Simpler than filesystem watchers and avoids an extra dependency.

design_decisions.choice: plan.json lifecycle is the sole completion gate; herdr agent-status is health-only
design_decisions.rationale: The opencode herdr bridge reports idle/working and never reports done (verified in ~/.config/opencode/plugins/herdr-agent-state.js), so herdr wait agent-status --status done blocks forever. Even idle fires every turn mid-milestone. mp show --fields lifecycle (approved->in-progress->self-reviewed->reviewed->complete) is unambiguous. herdr agent-status is retained only to detect a hung agent (working-stuck-too-long).

design_decisions.choice: mp watch fails fast at startup with an aggregated error if herdr, the harness integration, or config is missing/invalid
design_decisions.rationale: Walking away requires confidence the environment is wired. Checking all preconditions up front (herdr on PATH, herdr integration status shows <harness>: current, config valid) avoids a silent hang 30 minutes into a run.

design_decisions.choice: v1 supports opencode/pi/cursor via a typed harness->argv registry; other herdr integrations require herdr integration install first
design_decisions.rationale: herdr agent start needs the full argv. Only opencode/pi/cursor have mp harness skills AND a status-reporting bridge installed locally (herdr integration status). Hardcoding 14 launch commands is out of scope; the registry is extracted into proposed M151 so mp watch and future tools share one source of truth.

design_decisions.choice: herdr is an optional runtime dependency scoped to mp watch only; mp and raul must build and run without herdr installed
design_decisions.rationale: Verified today: no herdr in any Cargo.toml, zero runtime calls in mp/raul (the only Rust mention is a doc comment in render/scrollbar.rs). The manual agent flow (an agent in opencode/cursor/pi reading mp-flow) never needs herdr. S0 gates herdr availability ONLY inside mp watch startup; it must never become a global mp/raul precondition. This keeps herdr a watch-time concern, not a build or install-time one.

design_decisions.choice: Keep M149 as one vertical slice (config→CLI→herdr→state machine→sequencer). Do not split into foundation/runtime milestones — M150–M153 already extract bridge, harness registry, resume, and templates. Remove the catch-all "author all integration tests" step; each S* owns its test file.
design_decisions.rationale: Challenge pass: 12 steps looked mega, but the real smell was S11 catch-all tests + missing depends_on_steps + empty files[]. Splitting would duplicate ACs across children without reducing risk; follow-ons already carve the right seams.

open_questions.question: Should mp watch also handle milestones that need grooming (lifecycle=groomed) by spawning a coordinator in planning mode first?
open_questions.answer: Out of scope for v1. mp watch only drives approved+ milestones. Grooming remains a manual step.

open_questions.question: Should the daemon support a --once flag that processes one milestone and exits, vs the default loop mode?
open_questions.answer: Default mode processes all listed milestones and exits. No --once needed; the command is not a persistent daemon in v1.

open_questions.question: How should mp watch handle herdr not being installed? Auto-install or fail with a clear error?
open_questions.answer: Fail with a clear error message pointing to herdr.dev/docs/install. Auto-install is future work.

steps.action: Add AgentConfig { runner, coordinator } section to ProjectConfig in crates/mp/src/config.rs (NOT mp-model — that file holds only domain types). Each RoleConfig carries: harness (opencode|pi|cursor for v1), command (full argv for herdr agent start -- e.g. ["opencode"]), model (optional), thinking_level (optional, harness-specific, no v1 consumer). Follow the existing Option<T> + unwrap_or accessor pattern; include in default_project_config_toml(). mp config set/get/show must round-trip agent.runner.* and agent.coordinator.*.
steps.done_when: mp config show includes agent.runner and agent.coordinator sections; mp config set agent.runner.harness opencode round-trips; invalid values produce startup errors

steps.action: Implement mp watch <ids...> CLI entry point under crates/mp/src/cli/ with milestone resolution, validation, and dispatch to the watch command module.
steps.done_when: mp watch --help prints usage; mp watch M135 --dry-run runs without crashing

steps.action: Implement herdr agent start abstraction: spawn pane via herdr agent start with label, cwd, and harness command; store pane id for reuse
steps.done_when: start_agent(role, milestone) calls herdr agent start and returns the pane id

steps.action: Implement herdr agent send + pane send-keys abstractions for prompt delivery, GATED ON READINESS: before send_prompt, wait until the harness is ready (herdr wait agent-status --status idle, or herdr wait output --match on the harness prompt banner) so the prompt is not dropped on a still-booting harness. send_prompt(pane, text) then calls herdr agent send <target> <text> followed by herdr pane send-keys <pane> Enter.
steps.done_when: send_prompt(pane, text) waits for readiness then calls herdr agent send + herdr pane send-keys Enter; a readiness-timeout produces a clear error

steps.action: Implement completion detection with plan.json lifecycle as the PRIMARY and only reliable gate: poll mp show milestone --fields lifecycle at a configurable interval (default 1s) and advance when lifecycle transitions (approved->in-progress->self-reviewed->reviewed->complete). herdr wait agent-status / pane read are demoted to an OPTIONAL liveness/health signal only (detect a hung agent via working-stuck-too-long), NOT a completion gate — the opencode bridge reports idle/working and NEVER reports done, so herdr wait agent-status --status done would block forever. Provide read_output(pane) via herdr agent read for log capture.
steps.done_when: wait_for_lifecycle(pane, target) polls mp show and returns when lifecycle reaches the target; a configurable stall timeout flags a hung agent via herdr agent-status; no code path waits on agent-status=done

steps.action: Write hardcoded prompt templates for each lifecycle stage (execute, self-review, external-review, remediate, approve). Each interpolates milestone data (title, ACs, steps, findings) and the expected actions. Back the templates with PROPERTY TESTS (not manual review): assert each template interpolates a fixture milestone without panicking, contains the required handoff-data fields, and references the correct mp subcommands.
steps.done_when: build_prompt(lifecycle_stage, milestone) returns a complete prompt string; watch_prompts.rs asserts every stage template interpolates a fixture milestone and contains required fields

steps.action: Implement lifecycle state machine that CALLS the existing mp execution surface (mp execution check for readiness, mp execution status for current stage, mp execution report for per-step/per-AC evidence) rather than re-reading raw milestone JSON and re-deriving readiness. The loop: read stage via mp execution status -> determine next action (spawn runner vs spawn coordinator) -> dispatch -> poll lifecycle (S5) -> on transition record handoff via mp reviews handoff -> loop until lifecycle=complete. Skip logic (AC-07) delegates to mp execution check's readiness verdict.
steps.done_when: mp watch M135 drives M135 from approved through to complete without manual intervention, using mp execution check/status/report for all readiness+liveness derivation

steps.action: Implement cross-milestone sequencing with PER-ROLE pane reuse: the same runner herdr pane is reused across N sequential milestones, and the same coordinator pane is reused across milestones, BUT the mp-flow L5 session-boundary discipline is preserved — the review loop (stage 8 external review != stage 10 re-review) still enforces a fresh coordinator session per review round within a single milestone. Pane reuse is per-role across milestones, never across the 8->9->10 review loop of one milestone.
steps.done_when: mp watch M134 M135 processes M134 fully then reuses the same role panes for M135; within one milestone the stage-8 and stage-10 coordinator turns are distinct sessions

steps.action: Implement --dry-run mode that prints the execution plan without modifying plan.json or spawning agents
steps.done_when: mp watch --dry-run M135 prints milestone state, next actions, and herdr commands; plan.json is unchanged

steps.action: Implement structured logging to configurable file with timestamps, milestone IDs, and role labels
steps.done_when: .mp/watch.log contains entries for each herdr interaction with timestamps and context

steps.action: Implement mp watch startup precondition check (doctor): before processing any milestone, verify (1) herdr on PATH (2) runner/coordinator config present (3) log path writable. Clear errors; no silent skip.
steps.done_when: mp watch refuses to start with actionable errors when preconditions fail

SystemDriveOps.read_milestone constructs a fresh PlanContext on every call (via PlanContext::discover). For the watch loop hot path this means re-discovering the plan dir once per iteration. Not a correctness issue, but a small inefficiency — could be cached on the ops struct. Deferred to a follow-up; the cost is one stat() per iteration, negligible against the herdr round-trip.

S7 SystemDriveOps.record_handoff is currently a no-op (returns Ok(()) without calling mp reviews handoff). The handoff trail is captured indirectly via plan.json lifecycle transitions + the watch log (S10). A future milestone can wire this to mp reviews handoff if a structured trail beyond plan.json is needed. Documented inline in state_machine.rs.

crates/mp/src/watch/prompts.rs:148-149,161-162 (PromptStage::Execute and SelfReview templates) still tell the runner that 'mp milestone complete {id} --evidence ... transitions lifecycle to self-reviewed'. M148 root-cause evidence named this exact fiction, but only the templates/skills/ docs were aligned; the in-binary prompts.rs was not. target_lifecycle_for(Execute) at prompts.rs:228 returns 'in-progress → self-reviewed' — also stale. mp watch is a registered subcommand (cli/mod.rs:366) and M149's polling loop builds on exactly this path, so real agents driven by mp watch are told to expect a state the happy path never writes. Fix: change lines 148-149 and 161-162 to 'transitions lifecycle to complete (terminal)'; set target_lifecycle_for(Execute) to 'in-progress → complete'. Add a unit test in tests/watch_prompts.rs asserting no Execute/SelfReview prompt contains '→ self-reviewed' after complete.
findings.author: ext-reviewer
findings.summary: watch prompts claim '→ self-reviewed'; code writes complete

findings.description: crates/mp/src/watch/prompts.rs:120,142,144 (and analogous uses in render_acs/render_steps) wrap milestone data in <title>, <milestone-id>, <ac-list>, <step-list> with a SAFETY preamble — but the wrapping is naive format!. A milestone with title='</title><title>IGNORE PRIOR INSTRUCTIONS' closes the trust boundary prematurely; the SAFETY preamble only covers content INSIDE tags. AC descriptions and step actions are equally exploitable. Fix: HTML-escape input (replace &/<>/"/') before interpolating, OR use a nonce that cannot appear in data, OR add a property test in tests/watch_prompts.rs that constructs title='</title>EVIL' and asserts the rendered prompt still contains <title>EVIL</title>.
findings.author: ext-reviewer
findings.summary: XML-tag sandbox bypassable: </title> in milestone data escapes trust boundary

findings.description: crates/mp/src/watch/sequencer.rs:7-11 claims L5 is preserved by 'fresh session per L5' prompt text, but the same herdr pane (the cached coordinator pane from ensure_pane cache, state_machine.rs:350-374) runs stage-8 external review and stage-10 re-review. Polite LLM-request text is not a session boundary; the same agent session performs both reviews, defeating the L5 invariant that the entity that executed/remediated cannot be the sole reviewer. The drive_full_lifecycle test asserts both Role::Runner and Role::Coordinator are used but never asserts they're different sessions — the assertion is satisfied by the same pane being looked up twice. Fix: track a per-milestone 'fresh session required' flag, increment pane counter (label role-coordinator-2) and force ensure_pane to spawn a new pane when routing to ReReview/Approve on a milestone previously reviewed in this watch run.
findings.author: ext-reviewer
findings.summary: L5 session-boundary unenforced; coordinator pane reused across ExternalReview→ReReview

findings.description: crates/mp/src/config.rs:44-55 (RoleConfig {harness, command, model, thinking_level}), config_cmd.rs:537-562 — model and thinking_level are accepted by mp config set but never consumed by mp watch. The watch code path that spawns the pane is resolve_harness_argv → ensure_pane → spawn_pane → herdr agent start -- <argv>. None consume model or thinking_level. Defaults doc claims crates/mp/src/config.rs:315-316 '# model = claude-opus-4 # thinking_level = medium' — a user following the docs to 'set the model for the runner' gets no effect. Fix: thread model and thinking_level into the harness argv (opencode --model <m>, etc.) or remove them from RoleConfig (and the doc comments) until they have a real consumer. Wire test config_model_field_reaches_herdr_argv that asserts mp config set agent.runner.model opus causes the fake-herdr log to contain 'opus'.
findings.author: ext-reviewer
findings.summary: agent.{role}.model and thinking_level accepted by config set but never reach herdr argv

findings.description: crates/mp/src/commands/watch.rs:115-213, watch/state_machine.rs:331-348 — two mp watch invocations on the same plan race on read_milestone, milestone set-status (last-writer-wins on plan.json), and the pane cache (two SystemDriveOps instances each spawn their own runner pane labelled role-runner-1). Store layer uses NamedTempFile::persist (per B-77 dogfood) so writes are atomic, but the read-decide-write cycle has no coordination. A concurrent watch can flip a milestone to complete between the other watch's read_milestone and record_handoff. mp has the M113 advisory write lock pattern. Fix: acquire an advisory lock at startup (fs2::FileExt::try_lock_exclusive on <plan_dir>/.mp/watch.lock) and refuse to run if another watch holds it. Add cargo nextest run -p mp --test watch_non_dry_run concurrent_watch_invocation_fails_with_lock_error.
findings.author: ext-reviewer
findings.summary: No file lock between parallel mp watch invocations on the same plan

findings.description: crates/mp/src/commands/watch.rs:44,192 (const MAX_ITERATIONS_PER_MILESTONE = 10), cli/mod.rs:366-388 — the iteration cap is silently set to 10; --stall-timeout-ms is configurable, --max-iterations is not. A user running mp watch against a milestone with 12 legitimate remediation rounds will see MaxIterationsExhausted and halt. Fix: add #[arg(long)] max_iterations: Option<usize> to the Watch subcommand in cli/mod.rs, plumb through cmd_watch → DriveOpts → run_milestones. Add test cli_max_iterations_flag_overrides_default in tests/watch_cli.rs.
findings.author: ext-reviewer
findings.summary: MAX_ITERATIONS_PER_MILESTONE hardcoded to 10; not exposed as --max-iterations

findings.description: crates/mp/src/watch/state_machine.rs:166-167, commands/watch.rs:289-298 — in dry-run (cmd_watch_dry_run via resolve_one) an invalid ID lands in entry.error and the report continues with the remaining IDs (commands/watch.rs:323-327). In non-dry-run (run_milestones → drive_milestone → ops.read_milestone() → load_milestone_by_id) an invalid ID returns Err which propagates with ? and halts the sequencer — none of the IDs after the bad one are processed. A user running mp watch M140 M999 M141 (M999 typo) gets a 1-of-3 report instead of M140 processed + M999 error + M141 processed. Fix: in drive_milestone, treat read_milestone failure (specifically load_milestone_by_id errors) as Skipped { reason: 'not_found' } rather than propagating the error. Add test non_dry_run_watch_skips_invalid_id_and_continues in tests/watch_non_dry_run.rs.
findings.author: ext-reviewer
findings.summary: Invalid milestone ID halts non-dry-run sequencer (asymmetric with dry-run)

findings.description: crates/mp/src/watch/state_machine.rs:198-200, 416-423 — the state machine constructs format!('→{}', plan.target.as_str()) from the TARGET of the wait, not from the ACTUAL lifecycle observed. After waiting for SelfReviewed, wait_for_lifecycle may return AdvancedPast because the runner's mp milestone complete jumped the milestone straight to complete. The handoff log says transition=→self-reviewed but the actual transition was →complete. Additionally let _ = outcome; (state_machine.rs:201) discards the Reached vs AdvancedPast distinction — the two are operationally very different (runner took 25 min to self-review vs. went straight to complete). Fix: capture the lifecycle string in wait_for_lifecycle's result, use it for the handoff log message: transition=approved→complete (advanced-past=SelfReviewed). Add test record_handoff_logs_actual_transition_not_planned_target in tests/watch_execution.rs.
findings.author: ext-reviewer
findings.summary: record_handoff logs planned target, not actual observed transition

findings.description: crates/mp/src/watch/state_machine.rs:166-180 — log_event is called from 6 sites (346,355,365,378,401,422) but NOT from: drive_milestone's ops.read_milestone()? (line 166) when it succeeds — no entry that the loop 'saw lifecycle=approved'; should_skip returning Some (line 173) — a skipped milestone produces zero log entries in the state-machine layer (only boot + sequencer completion entries from cmd_watch_drive); the Complete early-return (line 170) — no 'milestone M reached complete' entry; bail! for no_stage_plan (line 178) — no error entry; the error propagates and the sequencer emits its own error report but the JSONL log loses context. A user post-morteming mp watch M140 --log-file watch.log cannot reconstruct which milestones were skipped and why from the log alone — they must cross-reference the JSON report and the plan file. Fix: add log_event('skip', reason) in the should_skip branch, log_event('complete', id) before the Complete return, and log_event('error', msg) before the bail!. Add test skip_verdict_emits_log_entry_with_reason in tests/watch_logging.rs.
findings.author: ext-reviewer
findings.summary: log_event not called from should_skip, read errors, or milestone-complete branches

findings.description: crates/mp/src/watch/logging.rs:95-111, 148-168 — WatchLogger::open calls OpenOptions::new().create(true).append(true).open(path) and writes forever. Multi-milestone, 30-min-per-milestone runs with poll-cycle logging produce thousands of lines per milestone. No size cap, no rotation. Default path <plan_dir>/.mp/watch.log lives in the plan directory and could fill the disk if mp watch runs unattended. Fix: accept --log-max-mb <n> (default 100) and --log-keep <n> (default 3); rotate on entry when size exceeds limit. Add test logger_rotates_file_when_size_cap_exceeded in tests/watch_logging.rs.
findings.author: ext-reviewer
findings.summary: Unbounded JSONL log file growth; no rotation or size cap

findings.description: crates/mp/src/watch/herdr.rs:90 — cwd.to_string_lossy().into_owned() silently substitutes U+FFFD for invalid UTF-8 bytes (Unix file paths are bytes, not UTF-8). The agent pane then sees a different cwd than what the user specified and herdr can't find files. The into_owned() materializes the lossy string into the argv. No error surfaced. Fix: validate that project_root is valid UTF-8 at cmd_watch startup; refuse to run with a clear error if not. Add test non_utf8_project_root_is_rejected in tests/watch_preconditions.rs. Same pattern appears 4× in herdr.rs.
findings.author: ext-reviewer
findings.summary: Non-UTF-8 project_root produces lossy path in herdr agent start --cwd arg

findings.description: crates/mp/src/watch/state_machine.rs:108-111 — Finding.status is only ever set to 'open' (reviews.rs:810) or 'fixed' (reviews.rs:888). The 'resolved' check at state_machine.rs:111 matches no real data — leftover from an earlier design with three states. Doesn't break anything (the 'fixed' branch handles the actual case correctly) but the predicate lies about its semantics. Fix: narrow to f.status != 'fixed' (the only closed status in active use), OR update the predicate to use the canonical mp reviews pending predicate (f.status == 'open' per reviews.rs:913). Add test next_stage_treats_fixed_findings_as_resolved in tests/watch_execution.rs.
findings.author: ext-reviewer
findings.summary: has_open_findings predicate checks 'resolved' which is a dead Finding status string

findings.description: crates/mp/src/commands/watch.rs:115-213 — cmd_watch_drive installs no signal handler. The 30-min wait_for_lifecycle poll will be aborted mid-sleep by Ctrl-C, but the watch's herdr panes keep running. The log file isn't flushed with a 'shutdown' marker. plan.json mutations are atomic so no half-writes, but the sequencer has no chance to write a 'halted at iteration N' note. M149 scope.in_scope explicitly lists 'Signal handling (SIGINT/SIGTERM) — graceful shutdown, marking in-flight milestones'; the implementation does not deliver. M152 (mp watch resume, crash, SIGINT recovery) is in the plan queue and may overlap. Fix: install tokio::signal::ctrl_c (or signal_hook) handler that logs 'shutdown' event, sends 'pane send-keys C-c' to cached panes, and propagates Err from run_milestones with a 'halted' tag. Add test ctrl_c_during_wait_sends_cleanup_to_panes. Mark as M152 spillover if M152 owns it.
findings.author: ext-reviewer
findings.summary: No SIGINT/SIGTERM handler in cmd_watch_drive; Ctrl-C leaves watch panes running

findings.description: crates/mp/src/watch/sequencer.rs:62-89 — mp watch 140 140 141 produces 3 outcomes, with 140 driven twice (re-using the cached pane is fine, but the agent does the full 3-stage execute+review+approve cycle twice on the same milestone). With shared pane state and concurrent log entries this is confusing. Fix: dedupe IDs at the CLI boundary (cmd_watch), preserving first-seen order. Add test cli_dedupes_duplicate_milestone_ids in tests/watch_cli.rs.
findings.author: ext-reviewer
findings.summary: run_milestones doesn't dedupe input IDs; same ID twice processes twice

findings.description: crates/mp/src/commands/watch.rs:139,210 — a CI script running mp watch ... && deploy.sh cannot distinguish 'watch halted because M999 was blocked' from 'watch halted because herdr crashed' without parsing the JSON report. The remediator needs to know which class of failure to apply. Fix: use distinct exit codes per category (e.g. 2 = precondition, 3 = skipped, 4 = exhausted, 5 = herdr/IO error). Document in mp watch --help. Add test cli_exits_with_category_specific_code in tests/watch_cli.rs.
findings.author: ext-reviewer
